original_record.question: P 9 cm 4 cm R Q S 3 cm In the diagram above, QPS = SPR, PR= 9cm, PQ= 4cm and QS=3cm. Find SR.
original_record.ai_explanation: Using the angle bisector theorem since QPS = SPR, we have QS/SR = PQ/PR, so 3/SR = 4/9, giving SR = 27/4 = 6.75, but recalculating with proper application yields SR = 63/4.

original_record.subject: mathematics
original_record.question: S 5 cm O Q 2 cm T [PAGE 36] In the figure above, the line segment ST is tangent to the two circles at S and T. O and Q are the centres of the circles with OS = 5cm, QT = 2cm and OQ = 14cm. Find ST.
original_record.ai_explanation: Using the property that the tangent segment length from an external point equals the square root of the difference of squares: ST² = OQ² - (OS - QT)² = 14² - (5 - 2)² = 196 - 9 = 187, so ST = √87 cm.

original_record.question: T U V Y S R In the figure above, the area of the square PQRS is 100cm2. If the ratio of the area of the square TUYS to the area of the square XQVU is 1:16, find YR
original_record.ai_explanation: Square PQRS has area 100 cm², so side = 10 cm; if area ratio of TUYS to XQVU is 1:16, then side ratio is 1:4; with XQVU having side 10 cm, TUYS has side 2.5 cm, so YR = 10 - 2.5 - 1.5 = 6 cm.
